osc1: Core oscillator 1. WAVE selects the timbre (sine = pure, sawtooth = bright/buzzy, square = hollow, triangle = soft). FREQ sets the pitch. AMP sets its level in the mix. VOICES stacks detuned unison copies for a fatter sound; DETUNE spreads them apart (wider, chorus-like). FB adds self-FM feedback — raising it morphs a sine toward a sawtooth and, high up, into gritty inharmonic tones.
osc2: Core oscillator 2 (defaults an octave above OSC 1). WAVE selects the timbre (sine/sawtooth/square/triangle). FREQ sets the pitch, AMP its level. VOICES stacks detuned unison copies for thickness; DETUNE spreads them for width. FB adds self-FM feedback (sine → sawtooth → gritty).
osc3: Core oscillator 3 (defaults an octave below OSC 1, for body). WAVE selects the timbre. FREQ sets the pitch, AMP its level. VOICES stacks detuned unison copies; DETUNE spreads them for width. FB adds self-FM feedback (sine → sawtooth → gritty).
mixmode: Couples two oscillators for metallic / FM timbres. MODE picks the type: RingMod multiplies the two signals (bell-like, clangorous sidebands); FM makes one modulate the other's pitch (harmonically rich, can turn aggressive). SRC A / SRC B choose which two oscillators are coupled (always kept different). Disable the module to just add the oscillators normally.
sub: Sub-oscillator tracking OSC 1 an octave (or two) below, for low-end weight. WAVE picks its tone (sine = clean deep bass, square = growlier with more harmonics). LEVEL sets how much sub is blended in.
noise: Noise layer for percussion, breath and texture. TYPE picks the colour (white = bright, full-spectrum hiss; pink = darker, more natural/balanced). AMP sets the noise level.
stringkarplus: Plucked-string physical model (Karplus-Strong). PLUCK (or the spacebar) excites the string. FREQ sets the string's pitch. AMP sets its level. DAMP sets how fast the tone dies away (low = long sustain, high = short/muted). STR (stretch) detunes the overtones for a more metallic or looser character.
wavetable: Wavetable oscillator that scans through a table of waveforms. BANK selects the table; LOAD WAV imports your own. POS morphs through the table — sweep it for evolving timbres. FREQ sets pitch, AMP the level. VOICES adds detuned unison copies; DETUNE spreads them for width.
envelopeadsr: Shapes each note's volume over time. ATK (attack) = fade-in speed (0 = instant/percussive, high = slow swell). DEC (decay) = fall from the peak down to the sustain level. SUS (sustain) = the held level while a key is down. REL (release) = fade-out time after the key is let go. Disable for a flat, organ-like level.
lfo: Low-frequency oscillator that automatically modulates a target. WAVE sets the movement shape. TARGET picks what it modulates: Frequency (vibrato), Amplitude (tremolo) or Filter Cutoff (wah / sweep). RATE sets the speed, DEPTH the amount. Modulated knobs show a live ring.
arpeggiator: Turns a held chord into an automatic note sequence. MODE sets the pattern (Up, Down, UpDown, Random). RATE sets the speed (notes per beat). OCT extends the pattern across extra octaves. GATE sets note length (low = short/staccato, high = long/legato).
filter: Shapes brightness. TYPE picks Lowpass (removes highs → darker) or Highpass (removes lows → thinner). CUTOFF is the corner frequency where filtering begins. RESO (resonance) emphasises the frequencies right at the cutoff — high values ring or whistle. The cutoff shows the LFO ring when the LFO targets it.
distortion: Adds harmonic grit and saturation. TYPE picks the flavour: Soft Clip (warm, gentle), Hard Clip (harsh, aggressive), Foldback (buzzy, complex). DRIVE sets how hard it's pushed (more = dirtier, louder harmonics). MIX blends the distorted signal against the clean one.
wavefold: West-coast wavefolding — folds the waveform back on itself for bright, metallic harmonics. DRIVE sets how much folding (more = more added harmonics). SYM (symmetry) offsets the fold for asymmetric, hollower tones. MIX blends against the dry signal.
bitcrush: Lo-fi digital degradation. BITS reduces bit depth (lower = grittier, more quantisation noise). RATE downsamples (higher = more aliasing, harsher old-digital sound). MIX blends against the clean signal.
chorus: Thickens the sound with a modulated, slightly detuned copy. RATE sets the modulation speed; DEPTH how far the pitch wobbles (more = lusher, seasick). MIX sets how much effect is added.
delay: Echo effect. TIME sets the delay length (short = slapback, long = distinct echoes). FB (feedback) sets how many repeats (higher = more, can build up). MIX sets the echo level against the dry signal.
reverb: Adds a sense of space. ROOM sets the size (small = tight, large = cavernous). DAMP tames the highs in the tail (higher = darker, warmer). MIX sets how much reverb is added.
stereo: Pseudo-stereo widener for the mono engine. WIDTH sets how far the stereo image spreads. TIME sets the short inter-channel delay that creates the effect (larger = wider but more phasey).
oscilloscope: Live view of the output waveform over time — its time-base can be zoomed to inspect the wave shape.
spectrum: Live frequency-spectrum view of the output: how much energy sits at each frequency (bass on the left, treble on the right).
